title: The Network Adaptive Market Hypothesis: Detection, Attribution, and Network-Mediated Efficiency
abstract: arXiv:2611.09208v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We propose the Network Adaptive Market Hypothesis (NAMH), a novel extension of the adaptive markets framework that conceptualizes market efficiency as a network-dependent equilibrium emerging from long-memory predictability and cross-market information transmission. Using G20 equity indices and five commodity futures over 2001-2026, we identify Japan as the central information hub, while the United States primarily acts as an information broadcaster. Contrary to conventional expectations, systemic crises do not exhibit higher network spectral radii, challenging the assumption that crisis-related fragility necessarily manifests through increased network amplification. Instead, crisis-related spectral contributions are dominated by Australia and the United States. tldr: 提出网络自适应市场假说（NAMH），将市场效率视为由长记忆可预测性与跨市场信息传递共同塑造的网络均衡，并发现日本是全球核心信息枢纽，而系统性危机期间网络谱半径并未如传统预期般升高。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Network Adaptive Market Hypothesis (NAMH), conceptualizing market efficiency as a network-dependent equilibrium shaped by long-memory predictability and cross-market information transmission, and finds that Japan is the central information hub while systemic crises do not necessarily exhibit higher network spectral radii.
